findings.location: Paragraph where Ellie asks her grandfather (translation: “«Bestefar,» spurte hun. «Tror du du kan lede sangen ‘Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ neste søndag? ...»”)
findings.source_quote: “Do you think you could lead the song ‘Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ this next Sunday? I would really like to sing it again!”
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the quoted song title into Norwegian consistently. Replace the English title with the Norwegian rendering used for the hymn in the lyrics section, for example: «Tror du du kan lede sangen «Frelser, lik en hyrde led oss» neste søndag? Jeg skulle så gjerne likt å synge den igjen!» Preserve the surrounding quotation marks and HTML structure.
findings.translation_quote: «Bestefar,» spurte hun. «Tror du du kan lede sangen ‘Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ neste søndag? Jeg skulle så gjerne likt å synge den igjen!»

findings.location: Paragraph where the song number is announced (translation: “«La oss synge nummer 8 i Tillegget,» kunngjorde sanglederen. Ellies hjerte sang. De skulle synge hennes favorittsang. Bestefar hadde innfridd hennes ønske.”) — earlier in source Ellie’s expectation referenced the song by number and the English title appears elsewhere
findings.source_quote: Her favorite song was ‘Saviour, Like a Shepherd Lead Us’ and although she couldn’t read yet, she knew it was number eight.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure the narrative reference to the song title is translated into Norwegian (keep the song-number notation unchanged). For example: «Hennes favorittsang var «Frelser, lik en hyrde led oss», og selv om hun ennå ikke kunne lese, visste hun at den var nummer åtte.»
findings.translation_quote: Hennes favorittsang var «Saviour, Like a Shepherd Lead Us», og selv om hun ennå ikke kunne lese, visste hun at den var nummer åtte.
